briefs.source_chain: US strikes on Iranian targets near the Strait of Hormuz spike oil and European gas therefore energy-driven inflation/rate expectations push global bond yields to multi-year highs (reinforced by Barr's hawkish comment and Simkus at the ECB) therefore equities sell off across the US, Europe and Asia, with RBNZ and RBA also hawkish.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain: Iran strikes near Hormuz lift oil/gas, higher energy prices feed inflation/rate expectations, yields hit multi-year highs, equities fall, with Fed/ECB hawkish commentary and RBNZ/RBA action reinforcing the move.

distortions.what: Brief drops Bessent's comment that the Strait of Hormuz will be 'bypassed' via pipelines in two years, and the gilt move being partly a bank-holiday catch-up rather than pure reaction.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — these are secondary color the source itself frames as asides; the core risk-off chain is unaffected.

briefs.source_chain: Iran strikes/response and higher yields drive a risk-off European tape (S&P -71bps, oil/yields up) therefore GS lays out trade ideas within that tape: short EU gas consumers vs long power-price-sensitive utilities on the TTF spike, Buy DELL ($425 PT) after its AI-server guidance raise, Buy-upgrade Deutsche Bank on ROTE improvement, stay constructive on European equities on valuation/FCF yield, plus data points on BTC ETF flows and the CLARITY Act.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain and same trade calls, same figures for DELL, Deutsche Bank, European equities, and the BTC/CLARITY data points.

distortions.what: Brief says BTC ETF inflows 'broke a nine-session streak' but omits that the source explicitly notes the week itself still recorded $923m of net inflows.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — brief doesn't claim outflows, just omits a supporting figure; the flow read stays flow-positive-but-streak-broken either way.

briefs.source_chain: August ISM misses and its internals weaken, but regional survey trackers and the S&P Global PMI actually improve, so the desk reads regional manufacturing surveys as strengthening despite the ISM headline, while JOLTS/construction data and Q3 GDP tracking stay roughly on pace; separately, equities close lower Tuesday on the Iran-driven yields/oil backup with cyclicals underperforming defensives, and DELL beats and raises with shares indicated sharply higher after hours.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain and figures throughout, including the ISM miss, the survey-tracker/PMI divergence, JOLTS/construction/GDP data, ETF short positioning, the equity close, and the DELL beat.

distortions.what: Brief attributes cyclicals lagging defensives to the ISM print alone ('so cyclicals lagged defensives'), where the source ties the sector move to both the ISM print and the yields/oil backup from the Iran escalation.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — same sector-rotation conclusion either way, just a narrower stated cause.

briefs.source_chain: Yields and oil (Iran, fiscal, AI-issuance crowd-out, inflation, buyback scepticism, hawkish central banks including the BOJ) drive APAC/US/EU futures lower therefore the desk turns tactically cautious/neutral and takes profit on gold therefore it still expects an attractive Q4 setup on the manufacturing upturn and an Asia positioning reset plus resumed EM inflows/Korean buybacks therefore it keeps a regional preference long US and Asia vs Europe, with supercycle-theme longs and added index hedges.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain and same regional preference/trade structure, same Q4-setup logic and same Asia positioning-reset argument.

distortions.what: Brief cites Asia positioning falling '75th to 40th' percentile (from the report's front-page summary); a separate section of the same source states '75th to 32nd percentile' over a different window (mid-June to late-July). This is an inconsistency inside the source document itself, and the brief faithfully reproduces one of the source's own stated figures.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — both figures support the identical directional conclusion (positioning reset from stretched to below-average), and the brief did not invent either number.

distortions.what: Brief characterizes the Positioning Intelligence section as 'a positioning wrap on hedge fund de-grossing,' but that section's own forward-looking question is whether re-grossing (flows turning positive) is coming, and it notes gross flows are already bottoming and getting less negative.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — this is a passing content-coverage label buried in a list of 'the note also carries...' items, not a standalone directional call the brief asks the reader to act on.

briefs.source_chain: Systematic/vol-control positioning is already maxed (DB: vol-control at the 100th percentile; GS: $146.5bn net length at the upper end of its one-year range) therefore BofA shows these strategies SELL under every scenario — down, flat, or up (the note's own title is 'sell sell or sell') — so there is no incremental buying support left in any market direction therefore GS's conditional projections corroborate a large down-market unwind vs only modest up-market buying therefore buybacks near peak just as the September blackout expands removes the other main source of support, compounding McElligott's warning that the vol collapse is 'epic' and could produce trading losses.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain except BofA's up-market scenario is stated as '$9bn bought in an up market' rather than sold, so the brief's read becomes: heavy selling down, modest buying up (asymmetric but still some upside support) — which softens the source's actual point that BofA shows selling under every scenario with zero incremental buying support anywhere.

distortions.what: Brief states BofA's up-market systematic flow as '$9bn bought,' but the source's BofA quote is 'sell $9bn in an up market' — all three of BofA's scenarios (down/flat/up) are sells, which is the entire point of the note (titled 'Sell sell or sell'). The brief appears to have conflated this with a different, later data point from Goldman ('modest additional buying in an up market'), which is a separate bank's separate projection.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: Yes — a reader acting on the brief would believe systematic flows still provide modest buying support on further strength, when the source's actual claim (per BofA) is that these strategies sell in every scenario including up markets, meaning there is no buying support left at all. That changes the read on whether rallies have systematic-flow support underneath them.

distortions.what: Brief softens McElligott's warning of 'major trading losses' to 'possible' trading losses.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — tonal softening of a hedge word, not a change to the underlying warning.
